custom.beads_notes:
Findings (2026-02-14):
- ../Learning-Tactus has a dedicated Models chapter + example: chapters/07a-models.qmd and code/chapter-07a/10-model-naive-bayes-imdb.tac using Model.training + tactus train/evaluate.
- No stale agent result accessors found (no result.response/result.message).
- Agent declarations use a mix of styles:
  - model="openai/gpt-4o-mini" (no provider) in some baseline examples
  - provider="openai" + model="gpt-4o-mini" elsewhere

Potential follow-ups:
- Decide a single canonical Agent declaration style for the book; sweep examples + prose accordingly.
- Ensure the Models chapter describes optional extras (tactus[ml], tactus[hf]) and clarifies what gets persisted in the registry (artifacts + metrics + tags).
- Ensure mock-mode guidance is prominent: tactus test --mock should validate procedure logic deterministically; real training is optional.

Outline / writing notes (proposed):
- Standardize the Agent declaration style across book examples for cognitive load reduction (recommend: model="openai/gpt-4o-mini"; mention provider= is optional + supported).
- Models chapter (chapters/07a-models.qmd):
  - Add an explicit 'What gets installed' note: base tactus vs tactus[ml]/tactus[hf].
  - Make the 'learners workflow' explicit and interactive:
    1) tactus test --mock (understand procedure logic)
    2) tactus train --model ... (train + register)
    3) tactus models evaluate ... (measure)
    4) tactus test (real)
  - Add a short paragraph on registry tags: latest, candidate/<name>.
- Add cross-links between the Agents chapter(s) and the Models chapter so readers can choose the right primitive quickly.
